mechanism: Android TV exposes adb over Wi-Fi once developer options and debugging are on, and the TV asks once to authorise the computer. A coding agent backs up the package list, then runs pm disable-user on manufacturer telemetry, ad and content-row packages, which hides them without uninstalling so a restore script can reverse each step. It then installs a small native launcher and sets it as the default home. The per-brand bloat list is discovered by the agent at run time from the real TV rather than hard-coded.
claim: Debloats any Android TV over ADB and installs a tvOS-style launcher in about fifteen minutes with a coding agent.
why_not_testable: It needs a physical Android TV on the network, which Proteus does not have.
needs: An Android TV or Google TV with debugging enabled
one_line: A repo lets Claude Code strip ads from an Android TV over Wi-Fi by disabling packages with adb, reversibly, then swap in a clean launcher.
idea_why: pm disable-user over adb is a standard, reversible mechanism, and letting the agent discover per-brand packages avoids a stale list.
breakdown: Enable developer options on the TV, connect with adb over the network, and have the agent dump pm list packages and settings as a backup. It then proposes disable candidates grouped by purpose and asks before touching anything the owner might use. Next it builds the launcher APK and sets it as home, checking each step with screenshots pulled via adb. A person would sort out the physical TV access for each customer if this were offered as a service.
